competencies.goal: Translate facility conditions into scope, frequency, responsibility, and verification decisions.
Differentiate cleaning, sanitising, disinfecting, routine work, periodic work, and incident-driven work.
Consider material compatibility, finish condition, soil type, tool aggressiveness, and restoration versus cleaning.
Reason about traffic, touch points, odour, scale, replenishment, frequency, and inspection.
Separate soil removal, degreasing, food-contact hygiene, process controls, and site-specific food-safety requirements.
Consider textile type, soil, cycle, dosing, stain treatment, process verification, and equipment constraints.
Use approved cleaning and disinfection concepts without inventing antimicrobial claims or contact times.
Prioritise label, SDS, PPE, ventilation, dilution controls, incompatibility warnings, and local procedures.
Choose verification that matches the operational decision and avoid overstating what a checklist or visual inspection proves.
Produce instructions that can be taught, repeated, supervised, and escalated when conditions change.
Clearly distinguish general technical guidance, examples from foreign regulators, manufacturer requirements, and local law.
Discuss labour, frequency, downtime, consumables, and asset life using explicit assumptions rather than invented costs.
